question: Defects land at random on a wafer, on average one per 500 mm² chip. Roughly what share of chips have none?
answer: About 37%. Random defects clump by chance: some chips catch two or three, leaving others clean. With an average of one per chip, the Poisson rule gives e to the minus one, about 0.37, defect-free. Halve the chip to 250 mm² and about 61% survive, one reason large processors are now built from chiplets.
move: An average of one per box still leaves plenty of boxes empty.
trap: An average of one defect per chip sounds like every chip is hit.
reference: May & Spanos, Fundamentals of Semiconductor Manufacturing and Process Control, Wiley-IEEE Press, 2006
